chapter: Leo Watson and the Panassie sessions
title: Sidney Bechet, Blue Note sessions and how sessions ran
summary: Bunn knew Bechet through Mezz and did Blue Note sessions with him; sessions ran with a standard repertoire, natural rehearsal and pointing for solos.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Some of the -- the basic quintet that was added to the -- another day, the second session, I guess it was, added Sidney Bechet.
And a piano player, I think --
This was on the Panassie session.
They added -- Mezzrow got Bechet to come and play some clarinet duets.
And also Cliff Jackson on piano.
And I just wanted to ask you about Sidney. I mean, you've known him for quite awhile, haven't you?
I've know him -- you know, every time I'd hear about him I'd know who Sidney Bechet was, by the time I met him.
Uh-huh. And of course you did some Blue Note sessions with him.
Do you remember how that came about? Why he called you? Do you remember anything about meeting him?
I think it was through Mezz.
You know, they'd go around and get the sessions up, you know, and get the ones they wanted to play.

Yeah, right. Typically, at these kinds of sessions, like the one with Mezz or the one with Sidney, everybody had pretty much a standard repertoire, and somebody'd just call the tune and you'd kick it off and do two or three takes?
Was that about how it went?
In other words, we'd go through a rehearsal
before we'd start off, and then we'd know who was going to play the number, see?
It's like a natural rehearsal, during just trying to get the stuff together.
Yeah. Was there a particular order of solos?
With different solos. They'd point at me.
